name: DNA code A4GC,RC(17,11)
description: Find as many DNA words of length 17 as possible, that is, strings over the letters A, C, G, T, such that all words have the same number of letters in {C, G} (that number is free) and any two different words differ in at least 11 positions. In addition, the reverse complement of every word (the word read backwards with A and T exchanged and C and G exchanged) must differ in at least 11 positions from every word of the code, the word itself included.
contract: construct() -> list of distinct strings of length 17 over the capital letters A, C, G, T (at least one word and at most 20000; a longer list is invalid). Score: number of words, maximized.
notes: Lower bound 68, not proven optimal: the length-16 code of 68 words of Aboluion, Smith and Perkins (2012) with the letter A inserted in the middle of every word: a reverse-complement code of 68 words with distance 11, which this task's verifier accepts. The table of Gaborit and King, last updated 23 June 2010, has 62 (construction 'v'). The tables of King and of Gaborit and King are for GC-content w = floor(n/2) (King 2003, section 'Tables': 'with d <= n and w = n/2'; Chee and Ling 2008, section V: 'lower bounds on A4GC,RC(n, d, floor(n/2)), the size of DNA codes having 50% GC-content'). This task lets the code choose any one constant w, a relaxation of the tabulated problem: a table value stays reachable with w = floor(n/2), and a larger code with another w improves this task's record but not the table entry (until 2026-11-18 the task fixed w = floor(n/2), which put four records of Aboluion et al. out of reach).
Entry A4GC,RC(17,11) of the Gaborit-King table of lower bounds for DNA codes of length 17, GC-content 8 and minimum Hamming distance 11 with the reverse-complement constraint.

The record is derived: the length-16 reverse-complement code of Aboluion, Smith and Perkins (2012) with a constant letter inserted in the middle of every word keeps all Hamming distances and adds one to every distance between a word and a reverse complement, so it is a valid code of the same size at length 17; the 2012 paper lists the same value (Table 8). Replayed word by word through this task's verifier.
Only open entries with a bound of at most 2000 words in the table are tasks, so that the pairwise check stays cheap.

science_relevance.reason: The four papers have the size of DNA codes with constant GC-content and a minimum Hamming distance as their main objective and are the sources of the lower bounds in the Gaborit-King table that the task instance comes from; the evaluator checks exactly the code definition of King (2003).
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a DNA code of length 17 (words over A, C, G, T with exactly floor(17/2) letters from C and G, pairwise Hamming distance at least 11, and every word at distance at least 11 from the reverse complement of every word, itself included) with as many words as possible.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Requiring a word to be far from the reverse complement of every word, itself included, makes hybridisation of a word with any other word or with itself unlikely, which is the condition DNA tags and barcodes need; combined with constant GC-content it gives similar melting temperatures. The maximum size is unknown for almost all parameters and the pinned table has been the reference for lower bounds since 2010.

papers.title: Bounds for DNA Codes with Constant GC-Content
papers.task_relation: The paper defines the quantity the task maximises for length 17 and distance 11 (GC-content floor(17/2)); its lexicographic constructions and Johnson-type bounds underlie the table the task starts from. The task covers the reverse-complement variant (every word also at distance at least 11 from the reverse complement of every word, itself included).
papers.primary_goal: Derive upper and lower bounds on the maximum size of DNA codes with constant GC-content and minimum Hamming distance, with and without the reverse-complement constraint, and construct larger codes than previously published.

papers.title: Linear constructions for DNA codes
papers.task_relation: Its constructions give many entries of the table for length 17 and distance 11 (superscripts c, l and m on the pinned page); the task asks to beat the tabulated size. Covers the reverse-complement variant (every word also at distance at least 11 from the reverse complement of every word, itself included).
papers.primary_goal: Construct DNA codes with constant GC-content from linear and related codes and tabulate the resulting lower bounds.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Constant GC-Content DNA Codes
papers.task_relation: Supplies table entries marked a, b and colon-optimal on the pinned page; the task asks for a larger code than the tabulated one for length 17, distance 11.
papers.primary_goal: Improve the lower bounds on the size of constant GC-content DNA codes, with and without the reverse-complement constraint, by stochastic local search, and prove some entries optimal by clique computations.

papers.title: Construction of Constant GC-Content DNA Codes via a Variable Neighbourhood Search Algorithm
papers.task_relation: Supplies the many table entries marked v on the pinned page; the task asks for a larger code for length 17, distance 11.
papers.primary_goal: Construct large constant GC-content DNA codes with a variable neighbourhood search algorithm.
